patterns.title: Arrays & hashing
patterns.tagline: Find what matters. Remember what you have seen.
patterns.description: Hash maps turn repeated searching into fast lookups. Use them when you need counts, membership, or complements.

patterns.title: Two pointers
patterns.description: Move two indices through a sequence while maintaining an invariant. Particularly useful for sorted arrays and symmetric comparisons.

patterns.title: Sliding window
patterns.tagline: Keep the useful work. Move the window.
patterns.description: Reuse a running result as a contiguous range grows or shifts. Look for subarrays and substrings with a condition.

patterns.title: Stacks
patterns.tagline: Let the last thing guide the next thing.
patterns.description: A stack remembers unfinished work. Use last-in, first-out ordering for nested structures and next-greater relationships.

patterns.title: Binary search
patterns.tagline: Make every decision cut the search in half.
patterns.description: Search a sorted space by maintaining boundaries that always contain the answer. Decide precisely which half can be discarded.

patterns.title: Dynamic programming
patterns.tagline: Solve it once. Build on what you know.
patterns.description: Describe a result in terms of smaller results, then store those results. Start with the state, transition, and base case.

problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description: Find two distinct indices whose values add up to the target. You may return the indices in either order. Every input has exactly one valid pair.
problems.constraints: nums is an array of 2–10,000 integers; target and values are between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000.
problems.output: An array containing the two zero-based indices.
hints: For each value, what other value would complete the pair?
Store values you have already visited alongside their indices. Look up the complement before inserting the current value.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.description: Determine whether any integer appears more than once in the array.
problems.output: true if there is a duplicate, otherwise false.
hints: What information do you need to remember after looking at a number?
Keep a set of values. A value already in the set is a duplicate.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.description: Ignore spaces, punctuation, and letter case. Determine whether the remaining letters and digits read the same from both directions.
problems.output: A boolean indicating whether the normalized text is a palindrome.

input.text: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

hints: Compare the outermost meaningful characters first.
Skip non-alphanumeric characters and move the two pointers toward the center.

problems.title: Sorted Squares
problems.description: Return the square of every value in a sorted integer array, with the result also sorted in nondecreasing order. Aim for linear time.
problems.constraints: nums is sorted, has 0–10,000 elements, and each value is between -10,000 and 10,000.
hints: The largest square must come from one of the two ends.
Fill the result from right to left, moving the pointer with the larger absolute value.

problems.title: Maximum Window Sum
problems.description: Find the largest sum of any contiguous subarray containing exactly k elements.
problems.constraints: 1 ≤ k ≤ len(nums) ≤ 10,000. Values may be negative.
problems.output: The maximum sum as an integer.
hints: What changes when a window moves by one position?
Subtract the departing number and add the incoming one. Initialize the best sum using a real window.

problems.title: Longest Unique Substring
problems.description: Find the length of the longest contiguous substring with no repeated characters.
problems.constraints: text contains 0–10,000 ASCII characters. Spaces count as characters.
hints: Keep a window in which every character is unique.
When a duplicate arrives, move the left edge past its previous occurrence without moving backwards.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Decide whether every opening bracket has the matching closing bracket in the correct nested order.
problems.constraints: text contains only (, ), [, ], {, } and has 0–10,000 characters.
problems.output: true for valid nesting, otherwise false.
hints: Which opening bracket must a closing bracket match?
Push opening brackets. Each closing bracket must match the top of the stack, and the stack must be empty at the end.

problems.description: For each array position, return the first strictly greater value to its right. Use -1 when no such value exists.
problems.output: An array of next-greater values in the original order.
hints: Keep track of positions that are still waiting for a larger value.
A decreasing stack lets one new value resolve several earlier positions.

problems.description: Return the first index of target in a sorted array that may contain duplicates. Return -1 if the target is absent. Aim for logarithmic time.
problems.output: The first zero-based index of target, or -1.
hints: Finding a match does not mean you have found the first match.
Remember a match and continue searching to its left.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You can climb one or two steps at a time. Count the distinct sequences of moves that reach exactly n steps. For zero steps, count the empty sequence as one way.
problems.output: The number of ways as an integer.
hints: The last move must come from either one step below or two steps below.
ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2). You only need to keep the previous two results.

problems.title: Non-adjacent Sum
problems.description: Choose elements from an array to maximize their sum, without choosing adjacent positions. You may choose no elements.
problems.output: The largest possible sum as an integer.
hints: At each position, you can either take this value or skip it.
Compare the best previous sum with this value plus the best sum ending two positions earlier.
